source_text:
Πρῶτον πάντων πίστευσον, ὅτι εἷς ἐστὶν ὁ θεός, ὁ τὰ πάντα κτίσας καὶ καταρτίσας καὶ ποιήσας ἐκ τοῦ μὴ ὄντος εἰς τὸ εἶναι τὰ πάντα καὶ πάντα χωρῶν, μόνος δὲ ἀχώρητος ὤν.
πίστευσον οὖν αὐτῷ καὶ φοβήθητι αὐτόν, φοβηθεὶς δὲ ἐγκράτευσαι. ταῦτα φύλασσε, καὶ ἀποβαλεῖς πᾶσαν πονηρίαν ἀπὸ σεαυτοῦ καὶ ἐνδύσῃ πᾶσαν ἀρετὴν δικαιοσύνης καὶ ζήσῃ τῷ θεῷ, ἐὰν φυλάξῃς τὴν ἐντολὴν ταύτην.
thought_title: First commandment: faith in the one God
orientation: The Shepherd, the angel of repentance, now speaks. He gives Hermas the first of twelve commandments: believe in the one God who made all things, fear him, and practice self-control.
pass_a_gloss: First of all believe, that one is God, the [one] all things [who] created and set in order and made out of the not being into the being all things and all things [who] contains, alone but uncontained being. Believe therefore in him and fear him, [and] having feared exercise self-control. These things keep, and you will cast off all wickedness from yourself and you will put on all virtue of righteousness and you will live to God, if you keep this commandment.

choices.term: ὁ τὰ πάντα κτίσας καὶ καταρτίσας καὶ ποιήσας
choices.english: he created all things, set them in order, and made them
choices.why: The three verbs are distinct: κτίζω is the act of creation, καταρτίζω is ordering or arranging what was made, and ποιέω is the general making; rendering each separately preserves the triadic emphasis on God's creative work.
rejected: he who created and ordered and made all things
the creator and orderer and maker of all things

choices.term: ἐκ τοῦ μὴ ὄντος εἰς τὸ εἶναι
choices.why: The philosophical formula for creation ex nihilo; keeping the abstract nouns 'non-being' and 'being' preserves the metaphysical force rather than paraphrasing.
rejected: out of what did not exist into what exists

choices.term: πάντα χωρῶν, μόνος δὲ ἀχώρητος ὤν
choices.english: he contains all things, and he alone is uncontained
choices.why: χωρέω means to have room for or contain; the contrast between God containing all and being himself uncontained is the point, so the same root must be kept in English.
rejected: he holds all things, and alone is unheld
he encompasses all, and alone is unencompassed

choices.why: The glossary mandates 'self-control' for ἐγκράτεια; the aorist imperative here is the verb form, so 'exercise self-control' keeps the glossary term while rendering the imperative.
The dative τῷ θεῷ expresses the one to whom the life is directed; 'live to God' preserves the dative force rather than flattening it to 'live for God' or 'live before God.'

bible_refs.note: ἔκτισεν γὰρ εἰς τὸ εἶναι τὰ πάντα (he created all things into being) echoes ἐκ τοῦ μὴ ὄντος εἰς τὸ εἶναι τὰ πάντα
ἐξ οὐκ ὄντων ἐποίησεν αὐτὰ ὁ θεός (God made them out of things that were not) echoes ἐκ τοῦ μὴ ὄντος

pass_b_english: “First of all, believe that God is one. He created all things and set them in order. He made all things come to be out of what was not. He contains all things, and he alone is uncontained.

“So believe in him and fear him, and, fearing him, be self-controlled. Keep these things, and you will cast all wickedness away from yourself and put on every virtue of righteousness, and you will live to God, if you keep this commandment.”

checks.via: blind check of the tuned English, clean at round 0 (tune_check.py)

polish.changed: Clarified the conditional clause at the end by removing the dash and making the sentence flow naturally, while preserving every claim and Scripture reference exactly.

notes.why: Capitalized as virtue-name in section 3 but lowercase elsewhere; reader may miss it's the same concept.
notes.fix: Consistently capitalize as named virtue, or add note.
